title: MediaForge RISK_REGISTER.json (fields load-bearing to check_dependency_graph.py)
description: Describes only the fields tools/prompts/check_dependency_graph.py actually reads from docs/MediaForge/prompts/01-governance-audit/RISK_REGISTER.json: top-level entries[], and per entry entry.get('status') and entry.get('affected_prompt_range'). The real file also carries a top-level description string and, per entry, title/severity/found_by/found_at_commit/affected_prompt_count/affected_tracks/evidence/recommended_fix/scope_note/gate_condition/resolution -- none of which this contract validates. additionalProperties is left true throughout for exactly that reason.

schema_version.description: Pinned to the value the real file has today. Bump only when the real file's schema_version changes.

entry.description: Both fields the checker reads are accessed via .get(), i.e. optional at the type level even though every current entry happens to have them.

status.description: Deliberately not enum-restricted to ["open","resolved"]. check_dependency_graph.py's _cycle_is_tracked only special-cases the literal string "open" and treats every other value identically, so enumerating a closed status vocabulary would describe more than the code actually implements.

affected_prompt_range.description: Exactly a 2-tuple [low, high] of prompt ids, matching the len(rng) != 2 guard and _prompt_number parsing in check_dependency_graph.py exactly.
